---
title: "Classroom Labs"
subtitle: "Five classroom labs"
---

The numbered sequence starts with setup evidence for every workload, then adds an
authoritative inference study, checkpoint-producing training, comparison
boundaries, and portable grading. Each lab states its allowed changes,
deliverables, interpretation questions, and ten-point rubric.

| **Lab** | **Primary Question** | **Availability** |
|:---|:---|:---|
| [01: Suite health](01-health-check.qmd) | Is this installation ready for benchmark work? | Laptop preflight |
| [02: Inference trade-off](02-inference-tradeoff.qmd) | What did one controlled batch-size change do? | Supervised pilot |
| [03: Training trade-off](03-training-tradeoff.qmd) | Did a training change produce an acceptable checkpoint? | Take-home accelerator lab |
| [04: Result comparison](04-result-comparison.qmd) | Which comparisons are valid, and why? | Supervised pilot |
| [05: Assignment package](05-assignment-package.qmd) | Can a functional artifact be verified and graded elsewhere? | Laptop preflight |

Before assigning a `max` workload, use the [readiness matrix](../readiness.qmd)
to distinguish target-passing, target-gap, and blocked local work.
The initial [course-image budget](https://github.com/harvard-edge/cs249r_book/blob/main/mlperf-edu/docs/internal/COURSE_BUDGETS.md)
covers one CPU and MPS-requested `min` run for every workload.
Instructors must still publish authoritative `max` budgets for the workloads
they assign.
